# M2 benchmark re-run after the control-order correction (M3)

*Generated by `scripts/render_m3_conflict_order.py`.* The published M2 report ([`m2-results.md`](m2-results.md), `reports/m2/results.json`) is **unchanged** and is reproduced by `--control-order abstain_first`. This file is the same frozen benchmark (same hand set, same dev set, same caches, same thresholds, nothing retuned) with the corrected order: **a known conflict between active documents among the top-3 is reported before the abstention check**. That is also the order the frozen protocol (`docs/eval-protocol.md` steps 3–4) specifies; the M2 code had them the other way round.

Ranking metrics (Hit@K, MRR, Recall@K) are computed on the raw ranking and are **identical** in both runs. Changed values below are published → corrected.

## What changed, in words
- **Conflict detection on the 4 conflicting held-out tickets: lexical and hybrid 3/4 → 4/4** (TCK-8018 was masked by abstention). Vector and rerank were already 4/4.
- **Cost:** a conflict is now reported whenever a member of a conflicting pair is among the top-3 active matches, even when the ticket is unrelated or the match is weak. So some tickets that previously ended in `NO_SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` now end in `CONFLICTING_AUTHORITATIVE_EVIDENCE` (abstention on unanswerable tickets falls for every strategy; false conflicts on answerable tickets rise to 4–12% held-out). `EVIDENCE` outcomes on unanswerable tickets (false confidence) are unchanged.
- Why this direction is accepted: hiding a conflict is the unsafe error; surfacing one costs a human look. From M3 on, a CONFLICT outcome is treated by the policy engine as *escalate to a human*, never as authorisation. Nothing was retuned; thresholds and all other parameters are as published.
- Headline decision unchanged: ADR-0013 stands (vector + governance default; lexical as provisioning fallback).
